title: Pre-Purchase Ship Inspection Istanbul | Tuzla & Anchorages
description: Pre-purchase inspection in Istanbul for ship buyers: bulk carriers, general cargo ships and tankers checked at Ahırkapı, in Tuzla or at Ambarlı before the sale.
h1: Second-hand ship inspections for buyers in Istanbul: at anchor by the Strait, in Tuzla docks and at Ambarlı
intro: Istanbul is where many second-hand bulk carriers, general cargo ships and small tankers find their next owners, and where many of them can be seen: waiting at Ahırkapı for a Bosphorus transit, lying off Tuzla for a yard slot, in a floating dock or working cargo at Ambarlı. A pre-purchase inspection here adds measurement to the buyer's own look round: spot thickness readings, crack checks at hatch corners and brackets, hatch cover and crane checks, and running readings on machinery. The inspection team travels from India for each ship and boards through the seller's agent or the yard.

highlights.h: A dry hull when she is docked
highlights.p: Ships on the market sometimes reach Tuzla for repairs or a survey before the deal is done. A ship in a floating dock is the one setting where a buyer can see bottom plating, propeller, rudder and sea chests directly, provided the seller and the yard allow the visit.

Istanbul buyers often send their own superintendent to walk the ship. We work beside that superintendent, adding the thickness readings, crack checks and machinery readings a walk-round cannot provide, and agree on board which areas deserve the most of the limited time.

A ship waiting for her Bosphorus transit can be told to weigh anchor at short notice. The plan ranks spaces by what matters to the buyer, so holds and ballast tanks are seen first and the buyer hears the key findings before the launch returns to shore.

sections.h: Where can a buyer inspect a ship in Istanbul?
p: Location decides what the buyer can learn. At the anchorages, a ship waiting for transit or orders is boarded by launch, and the inspection covers deck, hatch covers, holds if she is in ballast, ballast tanks the crew has prepared, accommodation and engine room. In the Tuzla shipyard zone a ship alongside a repair quay offers easier access and shore services, and a ship in a floating dock shows her bottom and side shell dry. At the Ambarlı terminals a container ship or general cargo ship is inspected around cargo work, within the terminal's ISPS rules.

Yard visits need two consents: the seller's, and the yard's, because the yard controls hot work, staging and the dock itself. When a ship on the market is under repair, the repair specification and the work in progress tell the buyer a great deal, and gas-free certificates issued for the yard's own work can open tanks that would stay closed at anchor.
list: Ahırkapı anchorage, off the historic peninsula at the Marmara end of the Strait: ships waiting for transit or orders
Anchorages at the Black Sea entrance: southbound ships awaiting transit, for deck, hatch cover and ballast tank work
Anchorages off Tuzla: ships waiting for a dock slot, often in ballast with the holds empty
Tuzla repair quays and floating docks: repairs or a survey under way, with the yard's permits and the seller's consent
Ambarlı terminals on the European side: container and general cargo ships during port stays
Altınova yards in Yalova: a ship docked across the mouth of the Gulf of Izmit, covered on the same trip

sections.h: Which second-hand ships do buyers inspect in Istanbul?
p: Handysize and Supramax bulk carriers are the core of the market, many of them past their third renewal survey and heading for, or already in, Black Sea and Mediterranean trades. Geared ships predominate, because many of the ports they serve lack shore cranes, so cranes, grabs and crane pedestals feature in almost every inspection. General cargo and multipurpose ships with tween decks, small chemical and product tankers, ro-ro ships and the tugs and offshore vessels built or repaired at Tuzla make up the rest.

Their cargoes leave distinct marks. Grain, fertiliser, coal and steel products in Black Sea trades wear hold frames, hopper plating and tank tops in different ways. Ferrous scrap, which Turkish steel mills import in large volumes, brings heavy impact damage to tank tops and lower frames from grabs and falling pieces. Fertiliser and coal residues left in damp holds add corrosion at the frame brackets. A buyer who knows the ship's recent cargoes already knows where the inspection should start.

sections.h: What does a pre-purchase inspection cover on a geared bulk carrier in Istanbul?
p: Holds come first when she is in ballast: lower frames and brackets measured and examined at several heights, hopper and tank top plating read for wastage, and hold bulkheads and stools checked for grab damage and wastage near their lower edges. Topside and hopper tanks are entered if the crew has ventilated them and the master issues a permit. On deck, the cross-deck strips between hatches, hatch coaming top plates and coaming brackets, air pipe heads and ventilators are examined, because these are items port state control officers in the Black Sea and Mediterranean regions record so often.

The crew opens and closes the hatch covers so the buyer can see them work, while the inspection notes packing, compression bars, cleats and drainage. Cranes are run through hoisting, luffing and slewing while we look at the visible slewing ring bolting and hydraulic leaks and check pedestal welds for cracks, using magnetic particle testing on a patch the master allows us to clean. In the engine room, generators, pumps and the steering gear are measured while running, and a thermal camera is turned on the switchboards while they carry load.

sections.h: What do Istanbul pre-purchase inspections typically find?
p: The findings below recur on older ships changing hands in Istanbul. Each carries a different consequence for the buyer: some are the seller's to clear before delivery under most memoranda, others become points in the negotiation, and some simply belong in the new owner's first docking plan.
list: Wasted lower hold frames and brackets, with the thinning worst just above the tank top
Grab and scrap-impact dents and set-in plating on tank tops and hopper slopes
Coaming top plates wasted under the packing line, and holed air pipe heads and ventilators
Cracks at hatch corners, coaming bracket toes and crane pedestal welds
Distorted or wasted tween deck panels and their securing on general cargo ships
Ballast tank coatings breaking down at stringers and edges in the topside tanks
Generators and pumps with high vibration, and loose or overheated switchboard connections

sections.h: How do you plan a pre-purchase inspection around the Strait and the Tuzla yards?
p: Turkey requires visas for Indian passport holders, so the visa, not the flight, sets the earliest boarding date; tell us as soon as Istanbul appears on the ship's itinerary or the seller names a viewing window. The team flies into Sabiha Gökçen for Tuzla and the Anatolian shore, or Istanbul Airport for Ambarlı and the European side. The seller's agent books the launch for anchorage boarding, and for a yard visit the agent or the seller's superintendent registers the team with the yard.

Weather matters on the Marmara anchorages. Strong winds can stop launch boarding for a day, and a buyer working to a tight inspection period should weigh that before choosing an anchorage viewing over a berth or a yard. If the ship is due at Tuzla soon after the viewing window, it is often worth asking the seller whether the inspection can move to the dock, where the buyer sees far more of her.

Send the ship's name or IMO number, where she is and when, the buyer's priorities and any class records already received to info@atlantisndt.com, or use the form on this page, and say whether your own superintendent will attend.

sections.h: Example scope: a small chemical tanker in a Tuzla floating dock
p: Suppose a buyer is offered a small chemical tanker that is in a Tuzla floating dock for repairs when the inspection is agreed. The dock changes the scope. Bottom and side shell plating can be read from outside, the propeller, rudder and sea chests can be seen, and recent shell renewals can be checked against the repair specification. Cargo tanks that the yard has had certified gas-free for its own work may be entered with the seller's consent, giving the buyer a direct look at the cargo tank coating or stainless steel.

The constraints come from the yard. Hot work nearby can close a tank to entry, staging may be rigged only where the yard is working, and the main engine will not run while she sits in dock, so machinery readings are limited to equipment that runs on shore power. The plan is therefore agreed with the seller's superintendent and the yard's project manager before the team boards, and the report separates repairs already in hand from conditions the buyer would inherit after delivery.

codes: Norwegian Saleform 2012 and SALEFORM 2025 – Clause 4, inspections
IACS UR Z10.2 (bulk carriers) and Z10.5 (double-skin bulk carriers) – enhanced hull surveys
IACS UR Z7 – hull classification surveys; GOOD, FAIR and POOR coatings
ASTM E797 – pulse-echo contact method for ultrasonic thickness readings
ISO 17638 – magnetic particle testing of welds
deliverables: Summary of findings that could move the negotiation, given before the team leaves the ship
Condition of holds, tanks, deck and hatch covers, with photographs located on the general arrangement
Spot thickness readings on frames, hopper and tank top plating against original values
Magnetic particle findings at hatch corners, brackets and crane pedestals
Crane, hatch cover and machinery observations with vibration and thermal readings
Spaces not inspected and the reasons, with notes on the class records reviewed

faqs.q: Can you inspect a ship for a buyer while she waits at Ahırkapı anchorage?
faqs.a: Yes. The seller's agent books a launch, and the team works through a ranked list of spaces in case the ship is called for her transit. On a bulk carrier in ballast the holds usually come first, followed by ballast tanks the crew has prepared, the deck and hatch covers, and the engine room. Strong winds on the Marmara can stop launch boarding, so allow some margin in the viewing window if the memorandum permits it.

faqs.q: Is it better to inspect a ship in a Tuzla dock than at anchor?
faqs.a: If the timing allows, usually yes. In a floating dock the buyer sees the bottom and side shell dry, the propeller, rudder and sea chests, and any repairs in progress, and tanks certified gas-free for the yard's work may be entered with consent. The drawbacks are that the main engine does not run in dock and that the yard's work restricts access in places, so machinery readings are more limited than at sea.

faqs.q: Can your team work alongside our own superintendent in Istanbul?
faqs.a: Yes, and many buyers here prefer it. The superintendent walks the ship with the buyer's own priorities in mind while our technicians take thickness readings, crack checks, hatch cover and crane observations and machinery readings. As findings emerge we agree on board where to spend the remaining time, and the superintendent has the key results before the team leaves. The written report then gives the readings, locations and photographs for the buyer's file.

faqs.q: Will the classification society credit your readings on an Istanbul pre-purchase inspection?
faqs.a: No. A society credits thickness readings only from a firm it has accepted under IACS UR Z17, and Atlantis has applications in progress with DNV, Lloyd's Register and ABS but holds no such approval yet. Pre-purchase readings serve the buyer's decision instead, compared with the class status and last thickness reports that the classification society releases with the seller's consent, whichever society the ship is classed with.

faqs.q: What should we ask the seller for before an inspection in Istanbul?
faqs.a: Ask, through the broker, for the seller's consent to every space on the plan, for the agreed ballast tanks to be emptied and ventilated, and for the classification society to release the class records. The last thickness measurement report, the most recent dry-docking repair list, the register of lifting appliances, hatch cover test records and the port state control history on Equasis all help us focus the visit. Send what you have to info@atlantisndt.com.

faqs.q: Do you check cranes and grabs on geared bulk carriers before purchase?
faqs.a: We watch the crew run each crane through its motions, noting brake behaviour, hydraulic leaks and unusual noise, and examine the pedestal and jib welds that can be reached, with magnetic particle testing where a patch can be cleaned. Grabs carried on board are examined visually for wear and cracking, and vibration readings on the hydraulic power units can be added. Load tests and crane certification are matters for the maker or a competent person.
